post_title: The ₹100 Rule: How Small Daily Savings Add Up to ₹36,500 a Year
excerpt: Skip just ₹100 of one small daily spend and you set aside ₹36,500 in a year.
body: Think of one small thing you buy almost every day without much thought: an extra snack, a delivery fee, a second cup of chai. Skip just ₹100 of it each day.

₹100 × 30 days is ₹3,000 a month. ₹100 × 365 days is ₹36,500 in a year, without any salary hike. The trick is to move the ₹100 out the same day, with a quick UPI transfer to your savings account, so it never gets spent.

post_title: The No-Spend Day: One Day a Week That Adds Up
excerpt: Pick one day a week when you spend only on essentials, and watch the small savings add up.
body: Pick one day a week when you spend only on essentials: bills, groceries and your daily commute are fine. On that day, carry lunch from home, skip online shopping and make your chai at home.
If that saves ₹300 each week, it adds up to ₹15,600 in a year (₹300 × 52 weeks). Bonus: you start noticing which spends you don't miss at all.

excerpt: Arjun got a ₹20,000 festival bonus, and this time he decided where it would go before spending a rupee.
body: Arjun (an illustrative example) got a ₹20,000 festival bonus. His first thought was a shiny new phone. Then he remembered last year's bonus: gone in two weeks, with nothing to show for it.
So this time he split it before spending a rupee: ₹10,000 into savings, ₹6,000 for family, and ₹4,000 just for fun. He still enjoyed the festival, and his emergency fund grew without any stress.
The lesson: decide where a bonus goes before it reaches your wallet.

post_title: The 24-Hour Rule: A Simple Way to Stop Impulse Buys
excerpt: Before buying anything over ₹2,000, add it to a list and wait 24 hours.
body: When you want something that costs over ₹2,000, don't buy it right away. Add it to a list and wait 24 hours. Many urges fade by the next day.
If you still want it tomorrow, check that it fits this month's budget first. Skipping just one ₹2,000 impulse buy a month adds up to ₹24,000 a year (₹2,000 × 12 months).

post_title: Story: How Ritu and Sameer Saved for a ₹60,000 Family Trip
excerpt: Ritu and Sameer wanted a ₹60,000 family trip without a loan, so they divided the cost by months.
body: Ritu and Sameer (an illustrative example) dreamed of a family holiday next summer, costing about ₹60,000. They didn't want a loan, so they divided it by the months they had: ₹60,000 ÷ 10 months = ₹6,000 a month.
Every salary day, ₹6,000 moved automatically into a separate 'trip' savings account. Ten months later, they travelled with the full amount ready and nothing to repay.
The lesson: big goals feel small when you divide them by months.
action: Pick one goal, divide its cost by the months you have, and start on your next salary day.
